issue_context.title: `server.hmr.port` config not respected on server side
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Specifying `server.hmr.port` does not seem to work properly in non-middleware (default) mode. The browser attempts to connect to the specified port, but there is no server listening there.

I originally opened an issue for this at https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/3017 but this can be reproduced in the pure Vite Svelte template, not just in SvelteKit - and I also highly doubt that this is Svelte-specific.

In digging into the issue, as close as I think I got to the core of it was in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/src/node/server/index.ts and https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/src/node/server/ws.ts - Here `createWebSocketServer` is getting called with the `httpServer`, which then (if I'm understanding the code correctly), it attempts to reuse as the websocket server, despite the separate `server.hmr.port` that was passed.

I don't know where I'd suggest a change happen, but it does seem like a separate websocket server should be created by Vite if `server.hmr` is an object with a `port` and it does not include an explicit server instance in `server.hmr.server`.

### Reproduction

1. Start from the `svelte` template (non-SvelteKit)
2. Edit `vite.config.js` to include `server: { hmr: { port: 10000 } }`
3. `npm run dev`
4. Load app in browser

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 5.10 Ubuntu 20.04.3 LTS (Focal Fossa)
    CPU: (8) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10510U CPU @ 1.80GHz
    Memory: 8.84 GB / 12.32 GB
    Container: Yes
    Shell: 5.0.17 - /bin/bash
  Binaries:
    Yarn: 1.22.15
    npm: 8.1.4
  npmPackages:
    vite: ^2.7.0 => 2.7.1
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

```shell
[vite] connecting... client.ts:22:8
Navigated to http://localhost:3000/
Firefox can’t establish a connection to the server at ws://localhost:10000/. client.ts:28:15
[vite] server connection lost. polling for restart... client.ts:222:10
[vite] connecting...
```

comments:
In case it helps someone else - What I ended up doing here, since I'm running Vite inside Docker, was to use `server.hmr.clientPort` instead of `server.hmr.port` and then use Docker to map the `clientPort` to the one Vite was still using internally by default.

This isn't a helpful workaround if you're not using containers, though, or if the reason you wanted to switch ports was because you already had something on that port.

I'm still seeing the same issue with a pnpm override specifying Vite 2.9.0-beta.2 and following the repro I outlined above. The browser attempts to connect to `localhost:10000` and cannot make the connection and the page repeatedly reloads.

I'm looking at the documentation change that was part of #7282, and I'm not clear on what's being said. Is it an intended feature to be able to override just the port and let Vite continue to manage that (separate) HMR server itself?

review_comments:
Why not set default `hmr.port` value here?
```suggestion
  const hmrPort = hmr && hmr.port || 24678
```

…then this line can be removed entirely:
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/975d9cd7ee7967a71466d22c3217b1640d7d0e59/packages/vite/src/node/server/ws.ts#L47
@benmccann @aleclarson after this change, aren't we always creating a new server for HMR? I think the idea was to reuse the server except when the user explicitly sets an `hmr.server` or `hmr.port`

> after this change, aren't we always creating a new server for HMR?

@patak-dev No, the behavior is the same. I think your confusion speaks to the confusing nature of the original way this was written. :P

>  I think the idea was to reuse the server except when the user explicitly sets an `hmr.server` or `hmr.port`

A new server is only created when `hmr.port` equals `server.port` (or `hmr.server` is truthy)

To clarify, the only time a new server needs to be created is when `hmr.server` is undefined and the ports defined by `hmr.port` and `server.port` conflict with each other. I still maintain that my suggestion is the correct behavior. :)

I'm thoroughly confused all around at this point. Ignoring for a minute whether they're the same, I wonder what the intended functioning is. The `if (wsServer)` block that reuses an existing server - is that supposed to be called when the ports are the same or different? Both versions seem to check that the ports are different before reusing the existing server. But I'm not sure that makes sense? The configured `hmr.port` never ends up getting used in that case... Should that check be reversed?

@Conduitry I'd love an extra set of eyes and any help testing from you as well

If I understand correctly,
- the default port `24678` is [only used in middleware mode](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/0535c7077b66e735217b790749a1a6fb4d58a44e/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/clientInjections.ts#L30-L31). So assigning it at the top of this function could be confusing. Let's not do this. Adding a comment to avoid future confusion would be ideal.
- reuse the server only if the ports are the same - we need a `new WebSocketServer` call when a custom port is given;
- Many `||` and `&&` can be replaced by `??` and `?.` to improve readability.

we can't replace `&&` with `?.` because the type of `hmr` may be `false | HmrOptions`, so we need the `&&` to coalesce the type to `HmrOptions`. I rewrote as @patak-dev suggested below, which I think is a pretty clean way to write it
Ah, thanks! I only knew that `?.` can be used on `false` in JavaScript, but I didn't realize it could cause TypeScript issues.
